subject: poisson with iid random effects vs neg.binomial

messages.author: 833479854a80815e
messages.subject: poisson with iid random effects vs neg.binomial
parts:
Dear all,

I fitted the length of a dry spell at unobserved locations with the negative binomial distribution yielding satisfactory results. However, "nbinomial" is not in use anymore according to https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/likelihood-example.pdf
For comparison I would like to try out poisson distribution with iid random effects. According to https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-INLA.html Chapter 2.3.2 or 3.3.1 I need to compute the expected length of a dry spell. But how would I do this for unobserved locations where I dont know the expected value?

I started with
r<-sum(temp$Length_dry_spell)/sum(temp$Days_per_month)
temp$expy<-r*temp$Days_per_month

but I get an error to remove the NA's out of the sum. So how should this work for prediction?

Very looking forward to your answer.
All the best,
Corinna

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] poisson with iid random effects vs neg.binomial
parts:
I think the pdf you linked is just an internal example file and that’s what the “not in use” means. The actual nbinomial.pdf is at https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/nbinomial.pdf
Finn
